learnPageBusinessStructure.overview: You need to choose a business structure before you form your business. Your choice affects your taxes, your personal liability, and what forms you are required to file.

simpleWords.text: Owners are not personally liable for business debts
A hybrid between a corporation and a partnership
The business does not file separate taxes
Each partner (called a member) includes their profits on their personal tax return

advantages.text: Limited personal liability for business debts even if you take part in management
Profit and loss can be allocated differently than ownership interests
The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) rules allow LLCs to choose between being taxed as a partnership or a corporation

disadvantages.text: More expensive to create than a partnership or sole proprietorship
State laws for creating LLCs may not reflect the latest federal tax changes
Cannot get venture capital funding
Cannot provide employees with stock options

simpleWords.text: This is the most basic type of business to establish
You are the only owner of the company
You are responsible for its assets and liabilities

advantages.text: Simple and inexpensive to create
Report profits or losses on your personal tax return

disadvantages.text: Personally liable for business debts
Cannot give/share equity, limiting funding opportunities and potential partners

simpleWords.text: More complex than other business structures
Suggested for larger companies with many employees
Separate entity from those who own it, meaning it can be taxed (or sued) independently from its owners, known as shareholders.
They elect a board of directors to oversee major policies and decisions
Appoint officers who carry out the daily operations of the business

advantages.text: Limited liability for business debts
Fringe benefits, such as an employer-paid insurance premium, can be deducted as a business expense
Shareholders can split corporate profit among owners and corporation

disadvantages.text: More expensive to create than a partnership or sole proprietorship
Paperwork can seem burdensome to some shareholders
Separate taxable entity

simpleWords.text: When you form a corporation, your default tax status is C corp
Then, after you register your business with the state, you can elect to be taxed as an S corp with the IRS by filing Form 2553
Profits and losses pass through to shareholders' personal tax returns instead of being taxed at the business level
S-Corps are limited to 100 shareholders and one class of stock

advantages.text: Limited liability for business debts
Shareholders report their share of corporate profit or loss on their personal tax returns
Shareholders can use a corporate loss to offset income from other sources

disadvantages.text: Venture capitals aren't willing to fund S-Corps or any other pass-through entity
Income must be allocated to owners according to their ownership interests

simpleWords.text: Two or more people sharing ownership of a single business
The partners manage the business and are responsible for all debts and obligations
The details of this agreement should be written out formally to define the roles of each partner

advantages.text: Simple and inexpensive to create and operate
Partners report profit or loss on their personal tax returns

disadvantages.text: Partners are personally liable for business debts
Owner is personally liable for partners' or employees' actions

simpleWords.text: It is a type of C-Corp
Unlike for-profits companies, they have a mission to benefit the public rather than generating profit, including religious, charitable, educational, scientific, or social welfare causes
Because they serve the public good, it can qualify for tax-exempt status with the IRS

advantages.text: Personal liability protection
No federal or state corporate income tax for 501(c)(3) organizations

disadvantages.text: Fundraising can be challenging and is impacted by changes in the economy
Members of the board of trustees can't be paid for their service
You must manage a lot of paperwork and record keeping to remain compliant with the IRS and ensure that you are transparent about business operations

simpleWords.text: It has both limited and general partners
The general partners own and operate the business
Limited partners invest in the business but have limited liability and limited input in its management
These business types are not usually used for retail or services

advantages.text: No mandatory corporate formalities, such as annual meetings or corporate filings
Personal liability of limited partners is limited to capital contributions
Limited partners don’t have to pay self-employment tax as general partners do

disadvantages.text: General partners are responsible for their liability as well as the liabilities of any of the limited partners
Limited partners are silent partners and cannot participate in management
Limited partners can lose their status and be held personally responsible for business liabilities if they’re found to be actively involved in the management of the business

simpleWords.text: They are similar to limited partnerships, but in an LLP even the general partners have limited liability
They are not responsible for the malpractice of the other partners
These business types are not usually used for retail or services

advantages.text: The personal liability in an LLP is limited to your capital contribution
It is not required to maintain corporate formalities, such as annual meetings or corporate filings
All partners can conduct business for the LLP and participate in management duties
LLPs are pass-through entities, meaning the LLP doesn’t pay taxes for the business entity
Profits are “passed” to the partners and taxed as personal income

disadvantages.text: Any partner in the LLP that is actively involved in the management of the business can lose their limited liability status
